newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court turns down O'Dell death row appeal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court turns down O'Dell death row appeal.

text.p: A federal appeals court on Wednesday turned down a request for new DNA tests on behalf of convicted murderer Joseph O'Dell, who is scheduled to be executed later in the day, the Virginia Attorney General's Office said.
In Washington, O'Dell's lawyers filed a last-minute appeal with the U.S. Supreme Court seeking to stop the execution.
O'Dell's claim was "meritless," the Fourth Circuit Appeal Court said in a brief statement on the ruling.

O'Dell, whose cause has been taken up in Italy and championed by Pope John Paul II, is due to be executed by lethal injection at 9 p.m. EDT (0100 GMT Thursday) for the 1985 rape and murder of Helen Schartner of Virginia Beach.
O'Dell's lawyers, in their U.S. Supreme Court appeal, said state-of-the-art testing of semen samples recovered from the victim's body could conclusively prove his innocence.
"There is no legitimate state interest in denying Mr. O'Dell access to this evidence," they said.
